## 5. The decisive unresolved operation

The next result must realize the successful instrument in a finite-bandwidth device **with an error bound scaled to its success probability**.

A concrete physical starting point is a longitudinally coupled readout cavity,

\[
H_{\rm phys}
=\frac{\Omega}{2}X+GZ(a+a^\dagger),
\qquad L_{\rm cavity}=\sqrt{\kappa_c}\,a.
\]

Modulated longitudinal qubit–oscillator coupling is an established readout proposal. In the fast-cavity approximation,

\[
a\simeq-\frac{2iG}{\kappa_c}Z,
\qquad
L_{\rm eff}\simeq-\frac{2iG}{\sqrt{\kappa_c}}Z,
\]

giving \(\gamma\simeq4G^2/\kappa_c\), up to a known field phase. That approximation motivates the model; it is not yet a proof that the heralded recovery survives a real cavity. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

The decisive target is a bounded, finite-bandwidth implementation satisfying

\[
\boxed{
\left\|
\mathcal M_{\checkmark}^{\rm phys}
-
\mathcal M_{\checkmark}^{\rm ideal}
\right\|_\diamond
\le \varepsilon_{\rm dev}\,p_0,
}
\]

with explicitly paid switching time, receiver decoherence, filter errors, detector behavior, preparation and reset costs. An absolute approximation error that exceeds \(p_0\) is insufficient: postselection can magnify it.

At the \(20\%\) operating point, \(\varepsilon_{\rm dev}\le0.002\) would leave the complete conditional error below approximately \(0.01\), before subsequent storage errors. This is a concrete certification target. It must be obtained from the joint cavity–source–receiver dynamics or measured process data, not assumed from the reduced source master equation.

The other side of the same operation is its efficiency curve. The present guarantee requires excellent collection and detection for useful single-use success; at substantial loss, its high-fidelity success becomes very small. A stronger causal receiver must improve that tradeoff under the same source-access restrictions, or a matching obstruction must show where this interface cannot be useful.

**The full consequence remains conditional on that physical and comparative result.** What is now constructed is an explicit recovery instrument for the original unknown input, with finite local operations and a complete photon-loss budget. The next challenge is to preserve that instrument at an operating point that earns its place in quantum hardware.

I’m narrowing the search to mechanisms that could remove one of those requirements. The comparison will include the cost of building and operating the mechanism.

Two obvious directions have weakened under comparison: mechanical computing already has strong experimental precedents, and one Astra learning construction has a documented calibration bill far above direct measurement. I’m now checking whether a receiver can turn information leaking into an environment into a usable quantum channel with finite, causal hardware. The key question is whether it can earn the receiver operations that the channel theorem assumes.

A simple receiver construction has produced a promising finite-model result: two small receivers, coupled to successive portions of a driven dephasing output, retain entanglement with the input reference. The one-receiver version I tested did not. I’m now deriving the small-time behavior and checking prior work; the numerical result alone does not establish novelty or a useful communication rate.

The analytic check confirms the effect, including discarded output: for every fixed nonzero collection fraction, the two-receiver channel preserves a small amount of distillable entanglement at short times.
